Both cover the guidance contexts the target belongs to (DCC/ephrin attraction-repulsion, DSCAM/L1 adhesion, SLIT-ROBO midline crossing, semaphorin repulsion, axon regeneration). B does it in 17 themes against A's 39 heavily repeated ones; A's only extra is a mostly p75NTR dependence-receptor theme.

A keeps the Rho GTPase family context (the CDC42-subfamily GTPase cycles, effectors and actin/cell-motility themes), which is core for a RHOQ GTPase cycle. B places the target only in GLUT4, insulin and adipocyte themes and misses that context entirely.

Both cover the same contexts (sex-steroid and estrogen synthesis, adrenal corticosteroid synthesis and CAH defects, the HPA/thyroid endocrine axis, vitamin D/phosphate and retinoid CYP metabolism). B does it in 11 themes; A adds near-duplicate corticosteroid-defect and thyroid variants.

B covers the main brush-border contexts (podocyte/apical polarity, CDC42-Rho regulation of actin, apical membrane transport and tight junctions, CFTR/epithelial transport, canalicular apical transport) in 7 themes. A repeats these across 17 themes; its useful extra is a stereocilia theme, and it also adds weaker glomerular-development and pancreatic-lineage themes.

Despite more overlap among its small cAMP/PKA and Gi themes, B adds two important physiological contexts that A lacks: adrenergic control of heart rate and contractility, and monoamine (catecholamine/serotonin) neurotransmission. A gives only the cAMP signalling core, neuropeptide behaviour and the HPA/appetite axis.
